title: Getting a fully hidden toy takes a means-end link between moving the cover and the goal
summary: Moore and Meltzoff say that recovering a fully hidden object requires coordinating the act of moving the cover with the goal of getting the object.
body: In that 2008 search paper, Moore and Meltzoff say that to recover a totally hidden object, infants must grasp and move the cover and also coordinate that act with the goal of getting the object. They call the coordination a coordination of means and ends. They used a partly covered object as the check on whether that coordination was already available. The sentence is their description of the skill the hand must link to a goal. It is not the age result from the trials.

sources.title: Factors affecting infants' manual search for occluded objects and the genesis of object permanence
sources.author: M. Keith Moore and Andrew N. Meltzoff
sources.note: Supports their means-end sentence: manual recovery of a total occlusion requires coordinating removal of the occluder with the goal of obtaining the object.
